dedupe_keys.name: sentinel 1 and sentinel 2 flood mapping data pipeline

description: This Python repository prepares satellite imagery and labels for flood-water detection. Its sampling documentation describes querying high-precipitation events over the continental United States, cutting 4 km by 4 km tiles, and acquiring Sentinel-2 optical bands and Sentinel-1 radar observations through Microsoft Planetary Computer. Configuration and scripts support preprocessing, training and benchmarking with human-labelled water pixels. A modeller could adapt the ingestion and alignment steps to prepare flood-extent observations for hazard or infrastructure exposure studies. The project also links a separate Zenodo release of 146 hand-labelled Sentinel-2 tiles, which is drafted as its own data resource. The README includes future goals as well as implemented scripts; this review does not assert a fully validated operational flood detector. No imagery, labels, weights or code packages were downloaded, and no model was run. The repository licence file grants MIT-style software rights despite GitHub classifying it as Other. Copernicus, PRISM and any derived image data retain separate source terms. Related resources include the distinct Zenodo labelled dataset and original satellite feeds.
licence: MIT for project software; Copernicus and other source imagery retain their own terms.
